meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Viet Nam (national-level unitary jurisdiction; no separate sub-state corporate registry)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law doctrine with socialist-law influences, codified and administered as a unitary national system
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement establishing the ASEAN-Australia-New Zealand Free Trade Area (AANZFTA)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP, 2019)
EU-Viet Nam Free Trade Agreement (EVFTA, 2020) and EU-Viet Nam Investment Protection Agreement (EVIPA)
Bilateral Investment Treaties in force with approximately 60 counterparties, including Japan, South Korea, Singapore, the Netherlands, Germany, Italy, and China
Double Taxation Agreements (DTAAs) with over 75 jurisdictions, including Australia, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, the UK, France, Germany, and China

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law on Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing No. 14/2022/QH15 (effective 1 March 2023), as detailed by Decree No. 19/2023/ND-CP (1 March 2023); Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14; Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on Enterprise Registration (mandatory beneficial owner declaration in the incorporation dossier); Circular No. 09/2023/TT-NHNN of the State Bank of Vietnam on AML/CFT implementation; Decision No. 1438/QD-TTg approving the National Action Plan on Anti-Money Laundering; Penal Code provisions on money laundering (Article 324) and terrorist financing.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (POA) executed by each founding shareholder/parent entity authorizing the Vietnamese law firm and incorporation agent to file the enterprise registration application
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public office (Văn phòng công chứng) in the shareholder's country of origin, or the Vietnamese Embassy/Consulate abroad for signature certification in Viet Nam
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization: Viet Nam is not yet a contracting party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; the POA must first be authenticated by the foreign Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalized by the Vietnamese Embassy/Consulate in the country of origin, followed by certified Vietnamese translation inside Viet Nam

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of the passport of each foreign Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO), director, and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notary office in Viet Nam or the Vietnamese diplomatic mission handling notarization of foreign documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization of the original passport copy by the Vietnamese Embassy/Consulate after authentication by the foreign competent authority (Hague Apostille is insufficient unless the issuing country is an Apostille state and Viet Nam's membership status changes; current practice requires consular legalization)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of the foreign corporate parent (if any), together with its memorandum and articles of association and board resolution approving the Viet Nam LLC formation and UBO disclosure
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the parent company's domicile, e.g., Companies House, ACRA, or the Secretary of State registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the parent's jurisdiction is an Apostille state, obtain a Hague Apostille from its competent authority, followed by official Vietnamese translation and a notarized copy in Viet Nam; if the parent is in a non-Apostille state, follow full Consular Legalization via the Vietnamese Embassy/Consulate; both paths are accepted by DOLESA (Department of Consular Affairs) only with certified translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based AML/CFT screening under Article 15 of Decree No. 19/2023/ND-CP and Part III of Circular No. 09/2023/TT-NHNN: all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories must be screened against the State Bank of Vietnam's AML database, the OFAC SDN List, the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU and UK financial sanctions lists, and the domestic list of designated terrorist organizations issued by the criminal procedure authorities. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) — both foreign and domestic — trigger Mandatory Enhanced Due Diligence per Article 7(1) of Law No. 14/2022/QH15, including source-of-wealth verification and senior management approval; the applicant must obtain an independent third-party screening report (e.g., Dow Jones, Refinitiv World-Check, or LexisNexis) dated not earlier than 30 days before the registration filing date; adverse hits require a written compliance opinion and may, in the case of UN/OFAC designation, disqualify the filing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Registration Portal (Cổng thông tin quốc gia về đăng ký doanh nghiệp) — https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Article 38 of the Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 and Article 26-27 of Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP: the enterprise name in Vietnamese must contain at least two elements: (1) the legal entity type 'Công ty TNHH' and (2) the proper name. The proper name must be written in Vietnamese alphabet characters (with or without diacritical marks), digits 0-9, and the symbols '@', '.', '_', '-'; a foreign-language name (e.g., an English proper name) may be registered alongside the Vietnamese name and must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet; non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese characters) are not permitted in the statutory name; the Vietnamese transliteration must be pronounceable and must not be identical or confusingly similar to a name already registered in the national database; the foreign-name element must not be a direct copy of a name registered elsewhere in Viet Nam.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Bank', 'Credit Institution', 'Securities', 'Insurance', 'Asset Management', 'Audit' — prohibited without prior written approval of the State Bank of Vietnam or the Ministry of Finance
'Government', 'State', 'People's Committee', 'Vietnam' — sensitive tokens requiring prior ministerial approval and demonstrable state affiliation or concession

'Corporation', 'Group', 'Holdings', 'Conglomerate' — misleading tokens not appropriate to the single-member or multi-member LLC structure unless the applicant proves an approved corporate-group classification
'National Assembly', 'Quoc hoi', 'Cooperative', 'Partnership' — names conflicting with other legal entity types under the Law on Enterprises

Any name identical or confusingly similar (including homophones and merely grammatical variations) to an already registered enterprise, dissolved enterprise within 3 years, or a dissolved enterprise under bankruptcy proceedings
Any name infringing intellectual property rights, including well-known marks, per Article 39 of Law No. 59/2020/QH14
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Viet Nam does not maintain a standalone name-reservation procedure; the proposed name is examined automatically as part of the enterprise registration dossier filed on the National Enterprise Registration Portal. If the name is rejected, the applicant must: (1) receive a written notice stating the specific reason for rejection under Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP; (2) file an administrative complaint (Đơn khiếu nại) with the provincial Business Registration Office within 30 days of the rejection notice, pursuant to the Law on Complaints No. 02/2011/QH13; (3) alternatively, or in parallel, the applicant may submit a revised name on a new registration dossier with no additional statutory fee; (4) if the administrative complaint is denied, the applicant may appeal to the provincial Department of Planning and Investment within 30 days of the denial; (5) final judicial recourse is available through an administrative lawsuit at the provincial Administrative Court within 90 days of the appeal decision; there is no extension of the 30-day name clearance window, but the applicant may reserve a revised name upon refiling.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted — under Article 44 of the Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 and Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP, the registered head office must be a physical, lawful premise located in Viet Nam with legitimate use rights (lease contract, or certification of lawful status of the domicile); the address must be a real, existing address and cannot be a PO box, a virtual office address, or a corporate-service-provider mailbox without on-site presence. For an ISIC 7020 management-consulting and AEO supply-chain audit firm, a leased serviced office or a dedicated room within a residential building used for business is acceptable, provided the premises are physically accessible to authorities; full virtual-office status is not registrable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 20-30% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection in the first year of operation, principally by the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (verifying head-office existence) and the tax authority (verifying business presence); the likelihood rises to approximately 40-45% if the entity proceeds to obtain AEO certification under Customs Circular No. 38/2015/TT-BTC (as amended by Circular No. 41/2018/TT-BTC and Circular No. 55/2023/TT-BTC), because Vietnamese Customs performs physical site audits of AEO applicants' premises, security procedures, and digital supply-chain records as part of certification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Enterprise registration application fee for a foreign-invested limited liability company, including online dossier submission via the National Enterprise Registration Portal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Provincial Business Registration Office under the Department of Planning and Investment (DPI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff: Circular No. 47/2019/TT-BTC of the Ministry of Finance (VND 100,000, approximately USD 4-5, rounded for international wire reference)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and UBO declaration administrative charge (integrated in the registration dossier)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: National Enterprise Registration Portal / DPI Business Registration Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Nil statutory fee — name examination and the beneficial-owner disclosure (Part C of the application form under Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP) are processed within the single consolidated registration application

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the incorporation dossier, including the company charter, the lease agreement, and certified copies of incorporators' passports and UBO identity documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Public Notary Office (Văn phòng công chứng) licensed by the DPI in the city where the head office is located
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff pursuant to Circular No. 144/2016/TT-BTC of the Ministry of Finance, capped at VND 300,000 per dossier, supplemented by the prevailing market rate for document drafting (approximately USD 60 total)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization and official Vietnamese translation of foreign-origin documents (Power of Attorney, corporate certificate of incorporation, good standing certificate, and passports) — estimated at 3 instruments
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Department of Consular Affairs (DOLESA) of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Vietnamese Embassy/Consulate in the country of origin, plus a licensed translation service in Viet Nam
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular legalization tariff of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (approximately USD 30-50 per instrument, depending on reciprocity) plus certified translation at approximately USD 1.5-2.0 per page under prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic AML/CFT screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories via a third-party compliance data provider, including the written screening report for the incorporation due-diligence file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dow Jones Risk & Compliance, Refinitiv World-Check One, or an equivalent licensed screening platform; alternatively a local AML compliance consultancy acting as reseller
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for enhanced per-entity screening packages covering sanctions, PEP, adverse-media, and enforcement hits (approximately USD 250-300 per corporate group filing)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal counsel and filing agent fee, covering UBO piercing, structure advisory, name clearance, drafting of the company charter, and preparation of the enterprise registration dossier for the AEO supply-chain audit scope (ISIC 7020)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Vietnamese law firm (LLC advocate) in Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City acting as the ủy quyền registration agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard foreign-invested LLC incorporation with UBO disclosure and regulatory-consulting scope — typically USD 700-1,000 in the Vietnamese legal market excluding statutory fees

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 (Enterprise Law 2020), specifically Articles 22-27 (enterprise registration), 31 (name rules), 47-50 (legal representatives), 52 (registered office), 74-81 (limited liability companies, charter capital, contribution), and 188-195 (FDI enterprise registration); Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14, Articles 36-38 and 44-45 (investment registration and project implementation); Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on enterprise registration; Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP guiding the Law on Investment; Circular No. 01/2021/TT-BKHDT (registration forms and dossiers); Civil Code No. 91/2015/QH13 (notarization and powers of attorney).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Planning and Investment (DPI, Sở Kế hoạch và Đầu tư) of the province or centrally-affiliated city where the registered head office is located; central electronic portal: National Business Registration Portal (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn), operated by the Agency for Business Registration (Cục Đăng ký kinh doanh) under the Ministry of Planning and Investment.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Enterprise Registration (Giấy đề nghị đăng ký doanh nghiệp) — Form II-1 annexed to Decree 01/2021/ND-CP, submitted together with the Company Charter, the List of Members (Form II-2), the List of Legal Representatives (Form II-3), and the Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) for a foreign-invested limited liability company.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum charter capital applies to an ISIC 7020 management-consultancy LLC, which is not a conditional business line under the Law on Investment 2020 or the Law on Enterprises 2020. Charter capital is freely determined by the members, but the full subscribed capital must be contributed within ninety (90) days from issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate (Law on Enterprises 2020, Art. 75.2). Contributions by a foreign investor must be remitted from abroad into a Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) opened at a licensed bank in Vietnam, and every capital transfer must be evidenced by inward remittance records filed with the DPI and the customs/tax administration as applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST MEMBERS' COUNCIL / SOLE MEMBER RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY

Date and place: [dd/mm/yyyy], [full address], Viet Nam.

Adopted by: the sole member holding one hundred per cent (100%) of the charter capital (or by all members holding one hundred per cent of the charter capital), acting in accordance with Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 and the Company Charter.

WHEREAS the Company has obtained Investment Registration Certificate No. [IRC number] issued on [date] by [DPI];

WHEREAS the members wish to register the Company as a limited liability company whose stated business scope is management consultancy services under ISIC 7020, including Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) certification advisory and supply-chain compliance security auditing;

IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED, unanimously, as follows:

1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND CONTRIBUTION: The charter capital of the Company is fixed at [amount in words] Viet Nam Dong (VND [amount]), subscribed by the members in the proportions set out in the annexed Schedule of Contributions. Each member irrevocably undertakes to contribute its subscribed capital in full within ninety (90) calendar days following the issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate, by remittance into the Company's Direct Investment Capital Account at [bank name and branch], account number [number]. Evidence of each remittance shall be delivered to the legal representative for filing with the Department of Planning and Investment. Defaulting members shall be liable for losses caused to the Company under Articles 76-78 of the Law on Enterprises 2020.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered and principal head office of the Company is established at [full address], Viet Nam. The legal representative is authorized to execute or ratify the lease agreement, obtain the lessor's consent, and complete all premises-related registrations and fire-safety procedures.

3. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS: [Name], passport number [number], is appointed as Director / General Director of the Company and, in accordance with the Charter, shall serve as the legal representative of the Company before the business registration authority, tax authority, customs authority, banks, courts, and all private parties. [Name], passport number [number], is appointed as President of the Members' Council (where a multi-member LLC is constituted). The Director is vested with full power to sign and file the Application for Enterprise Registration (Form II-1), receive the Enterprise Registration Certificate, open bank accounts, appoint tax agents and legal counsel, affix the corporate seal, execute employment contracts, and effect all post-registration publications and filings.

4. AUTHORIZATION: The Director, or any other delegate appointed by the Members' Council, is irrevocably authorized to carry out every incidental step required for incorporation, including notarization, translation, fee payment, seal engraving, license-fee declaration, publication on the National Business Registration Portal, and opening of the Direct Investment Capital Account.

5. GOVERNANCE: All decision-making, quorum, board composition, and signature powers shall conform to the Law on Enterprises 2020 (Articles 47-50 on legal representatives and Articles 55-62 on the general manager) and to the Company Charter annexed to this Resolution.

6. EFFECTIVENESS: This Resolution takes effect immediately upon signature and binds all members, successors, and assigns, and survives any share/capital transfer.

Adopted on the date first written above.

[Signature block: Sole member / all members; witness; notarization]

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation (Tổng cục Thuế) under the Ministry of Finance; e-Tax portal: https://etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn. Customs authority for export verification: General Department of Vietnam Customs (Tổng cục Hải quan) via the VNACCS/VCIS e-customs system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The foreign-invested LLC first obtains a Business Registration Certificate (Enterprise Registration Certificate) from the provincial Department of Planning and Investment. Tax registration is completed automatically or within 30 days via the National Business Registration Portal, generating the enterprise Tax Identification Number (Mã số thuế – MST), which serves as both the CIT identifier and the VAT ID. No separate VAT registration certificate is required. Foreign investors must submit legalized incorporation documents, passport copies, and capital contribution undertakings. The LLC must subsequently register banking details, e-invoice accounts, and any branch/employee sub-codes through the e-Tax portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: The Vietnamese LLC is a resident enterprise taxed on worldwide income at the standard Corporate Income Tax rate of 20%. Pass-through treatment is not available under Vietnamese law. Foreign tax credits apply for foreign-source income; territorial sourcing rules apply to cross-border service income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Limited statutory elections: (i) election between the VAT credit method and the direct method based on bookkeeping standards and business type; (ii) election of Small and Medium Enterprise incentives where statutory thresholds are met; (iii) election of preferential CIT rates/tax holidays in approved investment sectors or locations; (iv) no check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections are recognized; consolidated group tax filing is not permitted.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Thuế Giá Trị Gia Tăng – VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Companies must register for VAT upon issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate with no minimum turnover threshold. Business households and individuals are required to register and declare VAT only when annual revenue exceeds VND 100,000,000 (approximately USD 4,000). Foreign contractors may additionally be subject to Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) withholding at source.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing under Decree 123/2020/ND-CP and Circular 78/2021/TT-BTC. All VAT invoices must be generated via certified e-invoice software and transmitted to the e-Tax portal in real time or within 24 hours of issuance. Invoice data must be integrated through API access to etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn; each invoice carries a digital signature and QR code. Tax-authority-coded invoices are required for lower-compliance taxpayers, while self-issued coded invoices apply to high-compliance taxpayers. No physical stamping is required; customs export declarations are cleared exclusively through VNACCS/VCIS electronic data interchange.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to (i) goods actually exported from Vietnam and evidenced by customs declarations, including EPE/export-processing transactions; (ii) services supplied to foreign organizations or individuals and consumed entirely outside Vietnam; (iii) international transport and related services. Eligibility requires valid export/service contracts with foreign counterparties, compliant VAT e-invoices, full customs clearance documentation, proof of payment from non-resident bank accounts, evidence that services were delivered/consumed offshore, and a clean tax-compliance status. Input VAT refunds for zero-rated exporters are claimable when the accumulated refundable amount exceeds VND 300,000,000, subject to audit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (e-declaration cleared in VNACCS/VCIS)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill evidencing physical export
Export/Service Sales Contract with foreign counterparty
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign-currency bank credit advice proving payment
Shipping order, container release evidence, and inspection certificates as required
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating positions are subject to intensive post-clearance audits and desk reviews by the General Department of Taxation and Vietnam Customs. Fraudulent zero-rating or refund claims trigger retrospective clawback of all refunded input VAT, plus statutory late-payment interest from the refund date. Administrative penalties under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP (as amended) range from fines equal to 1–3 times the evaded amount to suspension of e-invoice authority and loss of refund eligibility under Circular 80/2021/TT-BTC. Repeated or intentional violations may constitute tax evasion or smuggling under the Penal Code, carrying criminal liability, corporate sanctions, and revocation of AEO customs authorization. All supporting documentation must be retained for a minimum of five years from the tax assessment deadline.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (SBV; Ngân hàng Nhà nước Việt Nam) under the Foreign Exchange Ordinance No. 28/2005/PL-UBTVQH11 (as amended by Ordinance No. 06/2013/UBTVQH13), Circular 02/2021/TT-NHNN on Direct Investment Capital Accounts (as amended by Circular 22/2023/TT-NHNN), Circular 03/2025/TT-NHNN (effective 1 June 2025, replacing Circular 05/2021/TT-NHNN) governing export, import and other trade-related foreign-exchange transactions, Circular 15/2015/TT-NHNN (as amended) governing foreign-exchange derivatives, and the Law on Anti-Money Laundering No. 14/2022/QH15 with implementing Circular 17/2024/TT-NHNN.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: VND is a conditionally convertible currency. Current-account transactions, including cross-border payments for professional services such as AEO certification and supply-chain security audits, are convertible through licensed banks without prior SBV approval, subject to documentary verification. Profit remittance by a foreign corporate investor of a Vietnamese LLC is classified as a current-account item: the remitting bank requires audited financial statements, corporate income tax finalization certificates, a board/shareholder dividend resolution, and DICA debit documentation; there is no additional corporate-level dividend withholding because taxes are settled as CIT on net profits. The capital account, however, is restricted: FDI equity injections, shareholder loans, and external borrowings must be registered and routed through the LLC's dedicated Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA); equity withdrawal and loan repayments require DICA-authorized debits and underlying approval/registration documents. VND is not freely usable outside Vietnam; offshore NDF trading involving VND by Vietnamese residents is prohibited and no formal onshore VND NDF market exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For the LLC's service exports (AEO certification and supply-chain audit fees), Circular 03/2025/TT-NHNN mandates repatriation of export proceeds into Vietnam within 180 days from completion of the service (date of invoice or service delivery), or such extended tenor not exceeding 365 days as the authorized bank approves on documented commercial grounds. Proceeds must be credited to the LLC's foreign-currency account at a licensed resident bank or directly to the LLC's DICA. There is no statutory percentage-based forced conversion/surrender requirement for FDI exporters: the LLC may retain foreign currency in licensed accounts but must use or sell it only through licensed banks for permitted purposes; conversion into VND occurs at the bank's regulated interbank rate with a disclosed spread. Documentary evidence at receipt: executed service contract, invoice, service completion certificate or audit deliverable, and SWIFT MT103 credit advice.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.profit_remittance_and_foreign_investor_p: Foreign corporate shareholders may remit dividends/profits annually after statutory audit, tax finalization, and adoption of the financial statements. The remittance is executed through the DICA or the LLC's foreign-currency payment account using an SBV-prescribed remittance form, accompanied by (i) audited financial statements for the fiscal year, (ii) tax finalization confirmation from the tax authority, (iii) board resolution approving dividend distribution, and (iv) proof of any transfer-pricing filings (TPR 01/02) if the LLC exceeds the related-party threshold. No separate SBV approval is required for current-account profit transfers, but the bank must classify the payment correctly and the LLC must retain the remittance dossier for five years. Prohibition: dividends may not be remitted before the annual audit and tax finalization are complete.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: WISE: Low-to-Medium feasibility as a regulated clearing rail. Legal constraints: Wise holds no intermediary payment service license under Decree 52/2024/ND-CP and is not supervised by the SBV as a payment institution; Vietnamese residents may not lawfully use unlicensed electronic payment platforms as the primary settlement channel for cross-border trade invoices, capital account movements, or profit remittances. Wise Business is acceptable only for incidental, low-value expense reimbursements via its licensed in-country correspondent banking partners, and never for DICA injections, dividend remittances, or statutory export-proceeds repatriation. Any Wise-generated VND payout to a Vietnamese beneficiary still requires a licensed local partner bank, and the accounting/audit trail must be reconciled through the principal bank relationship. Verdict: unsuitable as the sole or primary rail; acceptable as a contingency for staff travel and small consulting disbursements in USD/EUR, with full documentation in the treasury ledger.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is generally mandatory at initial corporate onboarding. Under SBV AML rules (Law on AML 2022, Article 12; Circular 17/2024/TT-NHNN), the bank must identify and verify the legal representative(s) and beneficial owner(s) by reliable means. In practice, Vietnamese tier-1 banks require at least one legal representative (or a Duly Authorized Representative holding an apostilled/notarized Power of Attorney plus the LLC's original seal certificate) to appear in person at the branch with original passport, Investment Registration Certificate (IRC), Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC), and company charter. Fully remote onboarding is normally reserved for Vietnamese citizens using chip-based ID/VNeID eKYC; for a foreign-director-only board of an FDI LLC, the standard expectation is an in-person visit or an on-site visit by the bank's compliance officer. Recommended approach: coordinate entry of one director to Vietnam with a pre-booked account-opening session at the chosen branch, followed by online banking activation and digital signing via e-token.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain opacity — the foreign parent/holding entity is located in a low-tax jurisdiction or the ownership chain is multi-layered.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle: (i) certificate of incorporation and constitutional documents for every entity in the ownership chain; (ii) consolidated share register up to the ultimate individuals; (iii) sworn beneficial-ownership declaration on the SBV-prescribed form under Law on AML 2022 / Decree 06/2023/ND-CP; (iv) notarized passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners; (v) corporate resolutions of the parent authorizing the Vietnamese LLC's account opening and over-the-counter banking authorities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the registered ISIC 7020 professional-services scope (AEO certification and supply-chain security audit) and expected high-frequency B2B settlements with logistics, customs brokerage, and manufacturing clients.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle: (i) executed AEO certification and supply-chain audit engagement agreements; (ii) sample deliverables, final audit reports, and AEO security verification certifications; (iii) invoice-workbook mapping client/contract/value/date; (iv) enterprise accreditation evidence (customs AEO status, ISO 28000 or equivalent certification); (v) annual business plan and client-concentration analysis; (vi) evidence of statutory professional liability insurance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Same-day high-value inflow followed by immediate outbound wires to third-country consultancy payees, creating a layering or round-tripping red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle: (i) board-approved treasury management policy including a 10-day settlement calendar; (ii) standing payment schedule tied to invoice due dates; (iii) bank-issued MT103 advice and trade reference mapping file; (iv) economic substance documentation of counterparties (business registration, VAT/tax ID, and professional licenses); (v) prior-period financial statements and cash-flow projections demonstrating a legitimate operating cycle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or prohibited-party nexus — counterparties or logistics entities in jurisdictions subject to UN/US/EU sanctions or appearing on global watchlists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle: (i) compliance attestation letter containing the enterprise-wide sanctions policy; (ii) consolidated screening output for each counterparty, director, and ultimate beneficial owner against UN, US OFAC, EU, and Vietnamese lists; (iii) transaction purpose letter explaining each supply-chain audit engagement; (iv) pre-completed enhanced due diligence (EDD) questionnaires from foreign clients; (v) commitment letter to freeze funds and file Suspicious Transaction Reports to SBV in accordance with Circular 17/2024/TT-NHNN.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient local substance for a professional audit firm — registered address is a virtual office or residential premises with no identifiable operational team.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle: (i) executed commercial lease agreement for office premises with utility bills in the LLC's name; (ii) staffing records (labor contracts, social insurance enrollment, personal income tax filings) proving resident employees performing AEO audits; (iii) certificates of professional competence of the audit personnel; (iv) professional indemnity insurance policy; (v) photographic/geotagged evidence of the operational office and equipment inventory.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All FDI equity contributions must be routed through the LLC's Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) opened at a licensed Vietnamese bank under SBV Circular 02/2021/TT-NHNN (as amended). Protocol: (1) obtain the IRC/ERC and open the DICA; (2) the registered foreign investor remits USD/EUR/VND via SWIFT MT103 quoting in fields 70/72: the IRC number, the registered charter-capital tranche being subscribed, and the BOP transaction category 'Foreign Direct Investment - Equity Injection (góp vốn đầu tư trực tiếp)'; (3) the bank verifies that the remitter is exactly the investor named in the IRC, that the amount does not exceed the unsubscribed portion of registered charter capital, and that source-of-funds documents (shareholder approval, board resolution, funding source evidence) are attached; (4) any FX conversion to VND is executed at the bank's regulated interbank rate with disclosed fees; (5) funds are released only for the LLC's authorized use-of-capital purposes as declared in the investment file; (6) the bank and the LLC jointly file the SBV-prescribed monthly/quarterly foreign-exchange/BOP reports; (7) shareholders' loans, if deployed, require separate registration with SBV and must flow through the DICA or a separate loan account. Non-compliance (e.g., remittance from a non-registered affiliate or amount exceeding registered capital) will result in rejection or forced refund of the wire.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The LLC's outbound settlements for imported consulting services (international AEO bodies, logistics software, specialized security audit sub-contractors) are executed via SWIFT MT103/MT202 cover from its USD or VND accounts, supported by: (i) executed service contract; (ii) vendor invoice; (iii) certificate of services rendered/deliverable acceptance; and (iv) evidence of Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) compliance under Circular 80/2021/TT-BTC (withholding on payments to non-residents). Domestic vendor payments in VND use the bank's bulk payment portal and NAPAS 247 real-time clearing; USD-denominated domestic payments are permitted only through licensed banks and cannot be settled informally. Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700) are generally inapplicable to the advisory/services business; however, standby LCs or performance bank guarantees may be issued at clients' request for AEO security audit mandates. Wise may be used only for de-minimis incidental international reimbursements (staff travel, small software subscriptions) after full reconciliation in the treasury ledger; it must never substitute for statutory export-proceeds repatriation or formal trade settlement rails. Every outbound disbursement must carry a valid BOP purpose code and be retained with the underlying dossier for five years for SBV and tax authority inspection.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable VND/USD forward contracts (tenor up to 365 days; underlying exposure from the LLC's export receivables or payable commitments; governed by SBV Circular 15/2015/TT-NHNN as amended).
Foreign-exchange swaps (VND/USD, tenor up to 365 days) used for working-capital conversion cycles and matching the maturity of underlying trade flows.

Foreign-exchange options (USD call/VND put or USD put/VND call, tenor up to 365 days) with premium paid in VND or USD; requires documentary proof of underlying exposure and prohibits naked/speculative positions.

Cross-currency swaps (VND/USD principal-exchange swaps) permissible for eligible long-term commercial exposures, subject to bank credit approval, ISDA/legal documentation, and SBV reporting obligations.

Permitted structured combinations (forward + option collars, participating forwards) of the above instruments provided the aggregate notional does not exceed the underlying commercial exposure and the structure remains fully deliverable; non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing VND are prohibited onshore for Vietnamese residents, and no speculative FX positions are allowed under Vietnamese law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax (CIT) Finalization Return (Quyết toán thuế TNDN, Form 03/TNDN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Department of Taxation through the General Department of Taxation eTax portal (electronic filing mandatory)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the 90th calendar day after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers, 31 March each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine of VND 5,000,000 to VND 25,000,000, plus late payment interest of 0.03% per day; prolonged non-filing triggers enforced tax collection, asset garnishment, and administrative deregistration (strike-off)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements (Báo cáo tài chính năm) and annual FDI Activity Report to the Department of Planning and Investment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Department of Taxation and the Department of Planning and Investment (for foreign-invested limited liability company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March (within 90 days after fiscal year-end, which is the statutory deadline for both the financial statements and the annual foreign-invested enterprise report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to VND 20,000,000 for late or non-submission of financial statements; compulsory filing order may be issued; repeated non-compliance contributes to enterprise status being deemed inactive and eventual administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business License Fee (Lệ phí môn bài) declaration and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial/city Department of Taxation of the enterprise head-office locality
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 January; newly incorporated enterprises pay within 30 days of issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate (first-year payment may be reduced by law)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest of 0.03% per day and late filing fines of VND 5,000,000 to VND 25,000,000; continued default subjects the enterprise to forced collection measures and possible deregistration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-annual and annual Investment Project Implementation Report for foreign-invested enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Planning and Investment of the province where the investment project is registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Semi-annual report no later than 30 July; annual report no later than 30 January of the following calendar year (in addition to the annual 31 March FDI activity report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Warning or administrative fine per Decree 50/2016/ND-CP; repeated failure to report may lead to suspension of investment registration and forced deregistration of the enterprise

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for all foreign-invested enterprises regardless of revenue or size under the Law on Accounting 2015 and Decree 174/2016/ND-CP; this foreign-invested LLC is therefore subject to compulsory annual statutory audit
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnamese Accounting Standards (VAS) and Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC for unlisted non-bank enterprises; IFRS voluntary for consolidated financial statements of qualifying parent entities

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Viet Nam has no standalone public UBO register or separate annual UBO confirmation form. The LLC must maintain an up-to-date Member Register reflecting all capital transfers and notify the Business Registration Authority within 10 days of any membership change; foreign ownership movements are also reflected in the certified FDI annual report. Internal UBO identification obligations apply under the Anti-Money Laundering Law to regulated reporting entities, not to ordinary non-financial enterprises.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Sổ đăng ký thành viên)
Register of Directors and Managerial Appointments

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Vietnam offers preferential CIT rates for eligible sectors: 10% for 15 years (e.g., high-technology, scientific research, education, healthcare, environment, software, renewable energy); 17% for 10 years (e.g., new industrial zones, agricultural processing). Qualified new investment projects in encouraged sectors and regions enjoy a 4-year CIT exemption and 50% reduction for the following 9 years. Additional tax deduction is available up to 150% of actual R&D expenditure for qualifying R&D centres. Standard auditing and compliance services (ISIC 7020) do not automatically qualify for high-tech incentives absent an express certificate from the competent authority.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly provisional CIT declaration: Form No. 01/TNDN. Annual final CIT return: Form No. 02/TNDN. Both are filed electronically via the national E-Tax Portal (https://etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn) or through supporting e-filing software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional returns and tax payments are due no later than the 30th day of the first month of each subsequent quarter (Q1 due 30 April; Q2 due 30 July; Q3 due 30 October; Q4 due 30 January). The annual final CIT return is due within 90 days after the end of the fiscal year (generally 31 March of the following calendar year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enterprise name, tax code (MST), registered head office address, legal representative, fiscal year dates, and the Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) / Business Registration Certificate numbers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign-invested LLC must use the Vietnamese MST and registered address as shown on the IRC. Attach certified copies of the IRC and Business Registration Certificate. Ensure the legal representative's name matches the latest trade registry notice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross sales revenue before tax from all business activities, including exports and service fees, stated in Vietnamese Dong (VND).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all revenue from Vietnamese and foreign clients; convert multi-currency receivables using the average interbank exchange rate announced by the State Bank on the transaction date. Reconcile the entry with the audited income statement where a statutory audit applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2 - Deductible expenses (Chi phí được trừ)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Actual business expenses supported by lawful invoices and proof of payment, directly related to generating revenue, excluding non-deductible items (fines, unsupported salaries, depreciation of non-business assets, and unauthorised provisions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses incurred in Vietnam and attributable to the LLC, properly documented under Decree 123/2020/ND-CP and Circular 96/2015/TT-BTC, are deductible. Intercompany management fees must be supported by detailed cost-allocation policies and contracts evidencing real services received.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 3 - Taxable income (Thu nhập chịu thuế)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total CIT-taxable income, arrived at as taxable turnover plus other business income, less deductible expenses, non-taxable income and losses carried forward from prior years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Carry forward prior-year losses for a maximum of 5 consecutive tax years. Do not claim exemption for foreign-source income unless a specific double taxation agreement or domestic law provision grants it and supporting evidence is retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4 - CIT payable (Số thuế TNDN phải nộp)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final CIT liability after applying the standard 20% rate, any preferential tax rates, investment credits, and after offsetting quarterly provisional payments already made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If claiming a preferential rate, retain the tax authority's incentive approval or notification in the file. Confirm that the actual activity under ISIC 7020 (AEO certification and security auditing) is described precisely on the IRC and is not merely an ancillary activity to obtain unintended tax incentives.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of quarterly or annual CIT returns triggers administrative fines: warning for delay up to 10 days; VND 1.5 million to 5 million for 11-30 days; VND 5 million to 15 million for 31-60 days; VND 15 million to 30 million for 61-90 days; VND 30 million for more than 90 days. Additionally, late payment interest accrues at 0.03% per day on outstanding CIT arrears from the day after the statutory deadline until full settlement. Under-declarations corrected voluntarily are fined at 20% of the additional tax amount; concealment or intentional misstatement can attract fines of up to three times the under-declared amount and criminal liability.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Vietnam does not impose a withholding tax on dividend distributions to foreign shareholders. After-tax profits may be remitted freely once the annual CIT finalisation is completed, any audit adjustments are settled, and creditor claims are paid.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Although dividend WHT is nil, double taxation agreement (DTA) relief remains relevant for interest, royalty, and technical service payments. To invoke a Vietnamese DTA, the non-resident beneficiary must obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its home-country tax authority and submit it, together with the official claim form (e.g., Form No. 02/HTQT per Circular 80/2021/TT-BTC), to the Vietnamese payer before the payment date. The payer then applies the reduced treaty rate at source. If tax has been over-withheld, the beneficiary may file a refund claim with the Vietnamese tax administration within the statutory limitation period (generally 5 years).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Under Vietnam's Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) regime: interest paid to a non-resident lender is subject to a 5% CIT withholding tax; royalty/licence payments to a non-resident are subject to a 10% CIT withholding tax (with VAT treatment depending on the type of service). Under the applicable DTA, treaty rates may be lower; common outcomes are 10% for interest and 10% for royalties, while certain DTAs reduce interest to 5%. Beneficiaries must present a valid TRC to obtain the treaty rate; otherwise, the domestic statutory rate is withheld.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: VND 30 billion (approximately USD 1.3 million) of aggregate related-party transaction value in a tax year triggers mandatory preparation of a Local File. Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required when the ultimate parent group's consolidated revenue reaches VND 18,000 billion (approximately EUR 750 million). Taxpayers with no related-party transactions are exempt from documentation requirements.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vietnam does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime comparable to the UAE. However, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under the Law on Tax Administration 2019 (Articles 75-77), together with Decree 132/2020/ND-CP, requires that controlled transactions be supported by real economic substance. A foreign-invested LLC must maintain an actual office, local employees, contracts, invoices, and decision-making functions in Vietnam. A mere shell or conduit company will be disregarded for tax purposes; the tax authority will re-characterise transactions, deny treaty benefits, and may recommend revocation of the Investment Registration Certificate under the Enterprise Law 2020.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration or concealment of taxable revenue; use of illegal or fictitious invoices (held-account invoices); unauthorised shifting of profits through shell entities; misclassification of distributable profits as deductible expenses; undeclared foreign-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: If the evaded tax amount exceeds VND 100 million, criminal liability under Penal Code 2015 (as amended) Article 200 applies. Administrative penalties include fines up to three times the evaded tax amount plus late-payment interest at 0.03% per day. In serious cases, fines up to VND 4.5 billion and imprisonment up to 20 years may be imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives who knowingly sign false returns or direct fraudulent receipt schemes are personally liable to restore misappropriated funds, may be subject to travel bans, and can be criminally prosecuted for tax evasion. The corporate veil is pierced where the LLC is used as a sham to perpetrate tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-compliance with the arm's length principle in intercompany transactions; under-pricing exports or over-pricing imports/royalties; failure to prepare, file, or maintain a transfer pricing file; refusing to cooperate during a tax audit; using undocumented financing structures to strip profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority will re-determine taxable income and assess additional CIT at 20%, plus late-payment interest. Failure to provide TP documentation allows the authority to apply its best estimate and can lead to penalties up to three times the undercharged tax. Incomplete documentation can incur penalties of 20-50% of the additional tax assessed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The CFO and legal representative may be personally liable for the additional tax where deliberate distortion of intercompany documentation is proven. Directors may face administrative fines, travel bans, and in fraudulent cases criminal prosecution for tax evasion. Civil restitution may be claimed by shareholders or creditors for breaches of fiduciary duty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: No Economic Substance - Shell / Conduit Company
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Vietnamese LLC solely for cross-border payment flows or treaty shopping without a physical office, local management, employees, or genuine supply-chain audit activity; overstating ISIC 7020 activities to obtain tax incentives; failure to maintain substance documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Expenses and offsets are disallowed, transactions are re-characterised, treaty withholding reductions are denied, and additional CIT plus interest are collected. The Investment Registration Certificate may be revoked under the Enterprise Law 2020 / Investment Law 2020 for sham business operations. Administrative fines can reach VND 200 million for continuing violations, and criminal penalties for fraudulent filing apply where amounts are material.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly responsible for company debts, their passports/exit visas may be blocked, and they may be prohibited from incorporating new companies if the entity is declared insolvent or fraudulent. Where profits are siphoned without proper corporate formalities, civil restitution for breach of fiduciary duty is recoverable personally.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Customs / AEO Compliance Failure (relevant to supply-chain audit scope)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misdeclaration of customs values in connection with related-party imports; false AEO audit attestations; inadequate record keeping; facilitating duty evasion for clients; failure to report related-party transactions in customs declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs penalties under Customs Law 2014 and Decree 128/2021/ND-CP include fines up to VND 200 million per violation; duty evasion can attract criminal liability. AEO certification may be suspended or withdrawn, resulting in loss of customs facilitation benefits and heightened inspection rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign customs declarations or AEO attestations may be held personally liable for customs duty arrears, subjected to travel bans, and in egregious cases prosecuted under Penal Code Article 188 (smuggling) or Article 200 (tax evasion). The corporate veil is pierced when declarations are knowingly false.
